title: Destroying Asteroids
summary: Given a planet's mass and an array of asteroid masses, determine if the planet can collide with and destroy all asteroids by gaining their mass if its mass is at least equal to the asteroid's mass; otherwise, the planet is destroyed.
statement: Given a planet's mass and an array of asteroid masses, determine if the planet can collide with and destroy all asteroids by gaining their mass if its mass is at least equal to the asteroid's mass; otherwise, the planet is destroyed.
constraints: Planet and asteroid masses are positive.
The planet destroys an asteroid when its current mass is at least that asteroid mass, then gains its mass.
Return whether some collision order destroys every asteroid.
hints: If the smallest remaining asteroid cannot be destroyed, no larger one can; if it can, taking it only increases future capacity.
Sort asteroid masses ascending and greedily consume each affordable one.
For asteroid in sorted list, fail if asteroid>mass, otherwise mass+=asteroid.
The exchange argument permits moving the smallest remaining asteroid first in any successful order without harming later feasibility.
editorial: The exchange argument permits moving the smallest remaining asteroid first in any successful order without harming later feasibility.

tests.explanation: Processing masses 3,5,9,19,21 lets the planet grow enough to destroy all.
After both fours the planet reaches thirteen, destroys nine to reach twenty-two, but cannot destroy twenty-three.
